conclusion.bottleneck: The current GPU/true-reference pipeline is constrained by shared CPU service, not GPU memory. The 31 allowed logical CPUs were 97%+ busy while this cgroup received about 14 CPU cores; the apparent 31-minus-14 difference is not evidence of idle CPUs.
conclusion.recommendation: Keep reference pool budget 28 and max_concurrent 16 for now. The CPU slot admission cap is binding at 10 tasks, whereas max_concurrent is not. Increasing process/pool counts on these already busy CPUs would add contention and is not supported as a safe throughput gain by this observation.
conclusion.runtime_alternative_not_applied: For a later controlled resource-only comparison, use two reference workers for new heavy tasks under the same total pool budget; more independent tasks may hide reference stragglers, but this audit does not measure that benefit. Do not interrupt active workers for this change.
conclusion.comparison_boundary: Rate is completed true reference cache misses divided by observed wall time, not isolated GeoSteiner function latency. Degree10 has much cheaper geometry and different search phases, so the overall net rate must not be interpreted as degree50 throughput. GPU utilization comes from four point samples rather than continuous duty-cycle integration.
limitations: No per-evaluate reference wall duration is instrumented in the current ledger.
The CPU analysis includes other workloads through host per-CPU counters, but no unrelated processes were modified or profiled by private command arguments.
The observation window covers early fixed-model training/evaluation; later calibrated-64 search can change the CPU/GPU balance.
